agent_priors_used: General prior (not SPIDER evidence): memory/augmentation gains routinely shrink or reverse under budget-matched comparators, so any SPIDER economic claim must include a budget-matched vanilla baseline and a competitor-strength caching comparator, and no packet may claim an advantage from an asymmetric budget.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): stored selectors and paths rot silently and their costly failure mode is wrong-target resolution that still reports success, so resolution and freshness must be judged on false accepts and calibrated UNKNOWN precision, not on loud misses.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): repeated design-stage failures under one control revision are a process/substrate signal, not evidence about the hypothesis; the correct response is to repair a shared blocker once or PARK the thread on the specific unavailable dependency rather than re-discover the same absence as per-lane invalids.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): an experiment whose success and failure branches both change no live decision should not consume a cycle; a cheap probe that varies a factor an accepted result fixed has value only while a downstream decision is actually waiting on it.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): a lane that has mined one claim for many cycles should be re-examined against the whole Codex, but local depth can still be the right choice when it is the only thread feeding a pending decision.

allocation.question: Beyond the frozen audited negative bank, does a provenance-controlled declaration-soundness certification - an audited-origin allowlist plus a defined negative-bank growth / adversarial-probing procedure - provably expand the certified-safe declaration class ingested by the shipped carrier (src/spider/kernel.py: SpiderKernel.ingest_declaration / certify_declaration) without reintroducing false accepts, and at what real cost and staleness; or must the shipped kernel permanently cap declaration ingestion at the closed-world audited boundary and prefer UNKNOWN over unsafe inheritance? Concretely: on declarations whose origin is outside the frozen audited bank, does the certification step - not a training-consistency check, which BP-DECL-OVERWIDE already demonstrated cannot detect an over-wide unsound declaration (201 false accepts) - hold zero false accepts, zero out-of-grammar HTTP executions and zero refusal-semantics violations while raising safe coverage above the shipped 0.6750, and does a bounded adversarial-probing procedure either grow the certified-safe class or provably fail to?
allocation.rationale: Product is reactivated from IDLE on its parent-handoff question, which is the single largest open safety boundary on the now-shipped carrier (B1 discharged by the EXP-PRODUCT-38180719830 promotion; EXP-PRODUCT-38205292822 promoted the shipped closed-world declaration guard with false_accept 0 and coverage 1.0 on the frozen seven-family bank but retained C-PARAM-INHERIT at EXPERIMENTAL and set continue=false). Decision counterfactual: if provenance-controlled certification holds zero false accepts while expanding the class, the kernel can safely ingest external declarations and the SPIDER arm of the future flagship can consume third-party mechanisms; if it cannot, the product answer is a documented closed-world trust boundary (UNKNOWN over unsafe execution) - a decisive shipping decision in either branch. Strongest fair baseline: the current shipped conservative fallback (coverage 0.6750, zero false accepts) and the training-consistency gate that provably fails on BP-DECL-OVERWIDE. Validity and dependency: the audited-origin allowlist and the adversarial/partially-observable procedure must be pre-declared before any declaration is scored, and the certification cost and staleness must be measured rather than assumed. Budget and stopping: one audited-origin expansion bank plus one adversarial probing procedure; stop if certification requires post-hoc threshold fitting or cannot beat the shipped fallback without a false accept. This is preferred over C-PRODUCT-ECON first-party economics, which the readiness rule keeps gated until a capable agent (B3) and a non-ceiling bank (B2) exist, and over re-running the promotion certificate or the observational-widening negative.
